title: Bro, why does everyone's AI make good looking 3D models but mine look like shit?
author: Jackster22
selftext:
I have tried to prompt ChatGPT and Kimi and Claude but keep ending up with absolute trash when it comes to the output.  
I have tried giving it reference material such as

https://i.redd.it/scdt8ffh7pyh1.png

  
But end up with something like. And this is the best it has done.

https://i.redd.it/o2dhw6wk7pyh1.png

Could someone actually link a working workflow on how to do this correctly please?  
I keep seeing amazing work being done but I have wasted a week's worth of ChatGPT tokens on this so far and getting trash results.

comments.author: Shadewarp
comments.body: I'm doing artwork/turntables (one image pr side) in Chatgpt, then use Tripo to generate the models (Claude doesn't build them) - then either rig the model myself or get claude to do it (takes a lot of tokens) and then bring it into my game.

replies.body: I'm not worried about token heavy, I've had claude, deepseek and chatgpt all use blender headless and with MCP server, it just generally doesn't produce any good results involving rigging/weight painting. I really just want it to be good at rigging/weight painting. I'm hoping that with the right workflow / tools it can get good at it. Or worst case scenario hoping the new fable 5.5 that's releasing will be better at it.

comments.author: Verdux_Xudrev
comments.body:
One, I wouldn't call any of those good, just that the top are easier on the eyes. Reminds me of the Saliens that Steam did a while back.

Two, try Image to 3d if you haven't already. If you can use a gen and then make them in Tripo or have your AI use that as a reference, it'll come out better. Think about it, if you take a random character from an anime or online and make a model from that, it'll look better. After that, some of the suggestions here are pretty good, but if you want something that looks more appealing, make a 2d image first.

comments.author: Fearless_Brilliant51
comments.body:
Throwing an image and asking AI to make this isn't gonna work unless you use image to 3D models. 

You need to make a 3D modeling skill for a specific style to get it to work better. Also stick to simple designs and nothing too complex. It could work, but atp just use an image to 3D model. Models with rounder/softer features are also harder to work with so keep that in mind.

Try iterating with targeted fix prompts and close up cropped screenshots of problematic areas. If you can't manage to get it to fix something with prompts than look up a blender tutorial, learn the basics and then try your best to bring the basic adjustment of what it couldn't to the model. Ask it to clean it up and learn and develop a skill to be able to do it by itself. 

It's not gonna spit out amazing models by just throwing in an image, it's a process that needs to be refined with iteration that requires less and less manual intervention as it develops 

Edit: Forgot to mention, let go of chatgpt and move to Claude opus 5.5 if you actually want to do 3D work
